articles.title: A multiplayer mod for The Last of Us 2 was reportedly cancelled "at Sony's request"
articles.summary: Development on a multiplayer PvP mod for The Last of Us Part 2 on PC has been halted after PlayStation got in touch and asked the developers to cease work on the project.
body: "Hey everyone, as you all know, the [The Last of Us Part 2] multiplayer mod that has been in development since January was supposed to [be released] this month," wrote modder Speclizer in a post on social media. "Unfortunately I recently received a letter on behalf of Sony Interactive Entertainment requesting for the mod not to be released. Extremely sad that this never got to see the light of day but I hope you'll continue to follow me onto the next project, this time something of my own."

If you were curious about what the mod what have looked like in action, Speclizer uploaded about 25 minutes of gameplay for the mod back in June. You can see the video below. Given that the team has spent nine months working on the project, the legal request from Sony no doubt stings - but what did PlayStation's legal team seek out cancellation of this mods when there are so many others out there? It may be because the team behind this one would have added a paid component to the mod, funded by a Patreon account - something that tends to get unofficial mods shut down.
points: Development on a multiplayer PvP mod for The Last of Us Part 2 on PC has been halted after PlayStation got in touch and asked the developers to cease work on the project.

articles.title: Blizzard confirms no more Diablo 4 expansions from now until Diablo 5's release
articles.summary: One of the biggest questions that emerged following the surprise reveal of Diablo 5 at BlizzCon over the weekend surrounded the future of Diablo 4. Blizzard announced a returning class - the Amazon - coming to the game sometime in the first half of 2027, but nothing beyond that.
body: Of course, the question on everyone's mind was whether the game will be getting any more expansions in the three-year wait between now and the 2029 release of Diablo 5. The studio's answer will likely disappoint many.

"We're all focused on [Diablo 4] seasons and getting to Diablo 5," Diablo game director Brent Gibson told PC Gamer. "We feel like we told the Story of Hatred. We had a great conclusion with Lord of Hatred with what we have with Mephisto, and we are moving towards telling the Story of Terror."

Lord of Hatred indeed had a great sense of finality, but I am willing to bet many simply saw it as the end of one arc rather than the game's entire story. Speaking of which, more story content is coming, but it will be delivered through upcoming seasons.

The events of Diablo 5 take place a century after Diablo 4 in a completely changed Sanctuary. It would have been nice to have a major Diablo 4 expansion serve as a narrative lead-in, but perhaps the 100-year gap is large enough to make that difficult. Still, Blizzard wants to do some of that work with seasonal content, but the developer doesn't quite know what shape things will take just yet.

Blizzard announced a returning class - the Amazon - coming to the game sometime in the first half of 2027, but nothing beyond that.

articles.title: Lanterns Season 1, Episode 5 Review & Recap: "Lights Out"
articles.summary: Lanterns wraps up its 2016 storyline with a real bang, as the situation in Rushville devolves into all-out war. Read our full review of Episode 5.
body: Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 5!

Lanterns is clearly a show intended to downplay some of the more ostentatious trappings of the source material, both for practical, budgetary reasons and out of a desire to tell a very specific kind of sci-fi detective story. This is not a series where Kyle Chandler’s Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre’s John Stewart are pulling out their rings and going hogwild with the energy constructs every few minutes. At most, you have to assume the people in charge are saving those flashier, more expensive scenes for a very specific time and place. Well, Episode 5 is that place, and it’s a wild ride.

articles.title: 'Marvel’s Wolverine' Voice Actor Reveals Who Inspired His Take on Logan
articles.summary: There’s no shortage of iconic Wolverine performances for actor Liam McIntyre to draw from. Hugh Jackman made Logan synonymous with his gruff, feral take on the character across the X-Men movies, while voice actors including Cal Dodd and Steve Blum have each put their own stamp on Marvel’s clawed…
body: Asked which previous versions of Wolverine inspired his performance, McIntyre gave a fairly definitive answer: all of them.

“It was every single one,” McIntyre said in an interview with Polygon while discussing his new animated series Golden Axe. “I had so many great teachers, from wonderful performance of the past, and trying to find your own sort of spin or take on it.”
For McIntyre, that meant looking at what made each previous interpretation of Logan work before figuring out how he could bring something of himself to the character.

“I would see Hugh [Jackman] and Cal Dodd and, Steve Blum and other wonderful performers and try to go, ‘Well, that’s such a great display of what makes Wolverine Wolverine. I’ll try and find the essence of that character as I can do it, because I can’t copy it,’” he said.

articles.title: After 'Reacher' Season 4 Ends, Here Are Alan Ritchson's 10 Best Performances to Watch Next
articles.summary: From American Idol to Reacher, these are the performances that turned Alan Ritchson into one of Hollywood's biggest action stars.
body: Every overnight success has an origin story. Alan Ritchson 's just happens to include Simon Cowell.

Long before he was snapping bones as Jack Reacher, in 2004 Ritchson was a 20-year-old aspiring singer auditioning for American Idol, where he survived the contest long enough to charm Paula Abdul before eventually getting sent home. Good thing he turned out to be better at throwing punches than hitting high notes. A year later, he traded microphones for muscles, making his scripted acting debut as Arthur Curry, aka Aquaman, on Smallville.

Looking back now, it's easy to forget that Reacher wasn't the beginning of Ritchson's career, but it was the payoff. He spent nearly 20 years bouncing between network dramas, cult comedies, superhero shows, blockbuster franchises, and independent action films before finally landing the role that made him a household name. With Reacher season 4 coming to an end on Sept. 16, these are the 10 performances that stand above the rest.

articles.title: New Batman: Part 2 Set Photos Hint at the Court of Owls
articles.summary: New videos and photos from the London set of The Batman: Part II show Robert Pattinson’s Bruce Wayne being escorted by police through a crowd of angry protesters. These images only further fuel the rumors that Gotham’s secret cabal of wealthy elites, the Court of Owls, factor into the story, but…
body: Footage on social media shows director Matt Reeves and cinematographer Erik Messerschmidt filming a scene where Bruce is protected by the GCPD as he exits down the stairs of the Gotham Bar Association past mobs of protestors to a waiting Bentley where he’s met by Andy Serkis’ double as Alfred Pennyworth. (Serkis is busy in New Zealand directing and starring in The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum.) Jeffrey Wright as Jim Gordon was also spotted on set.

The signs and placards waved by the protestors’ reveal the source of their anger and the first hint of the Court of Owls: “ Court of Oligarchs,” “Court of Fouls,” “The Richer Get Richer,” “One Day The Poor Will Have Nothing,” “ Re$i$t,” “Eat the Rich,” “Your Greed is Killin Us,” and “Oligarchs Gotta Go!.”
There are also signs bearing Batman imagery, such as one that reads “ Save Us ” and another that features the Batman mask with “I’m coming for you next” written below it.

The irony in these images, of course, is that the protesters clearly view Bruce Wayne, the city’s wealthiest man, as an enemy while embracing his alter ego Batman as a symbol of resistance against a corrupt system.

articles.title: 9 Sci-Fi Series on Netflix That Are Perfect from Start to Finish
articles.summary: But there are some shows on Netflix where this isn’t a problem and you can breeze through episode after episode without feeling like it's work to get back to the good stuff. Here are nine such sci-fi shows that are on Netflix right now, that are great from start to finish.
body: Far too often, when you’re watching a series on Netflix and you’re really getting into it, you reach a point where the show suddenly goes way downhill. (Or gets suddenly canceled with no notice.) Even if things improve again later, the lull messes with the overall experience. Stranger Things suffered a massive decline after season 3, while The OA ended on a massive cliffhanger.

Based on the book by Stephen King, 11.22.63 is an eight-episode miniseries about a time traveler trying to stop the assassination of President John F. Kennedy. Jake Epping (James Franco) is an ordinary English teacher tasked with the mission who ends up making all kinds of mistakes in the past, like getting too attached to the people there.

The show cleverly mixes classic sci-fi elements and themes and blends them with one of the best-known moments in American history, making the events and characters included take on a particular foreboding element. Especially interesting is the sense Jake gets that time itself is “pushing back” on his actions, as though what’s about to happen is supposed to happen and his mission may very well be hopeless.

articles.title: Diablo 5 Director Confirms Game is Already in Full Production
articles.summary: Diablo 5 is officially in full production and coming in 2029. Game Director Joe Shely reveals the sequel will feature more classes, procedural worlds, and jump 100 years into the future.
body: While tons of new updates are coming to Diablo, including a new Netflix series, Diablo 4 Season 15, a Switch 2 port, and more, the biggest reveal for the franchise at BlizzCon 2026 was the announcement of Diablo V, coming in 2029.

IGN sat down exclusively with the team behind the upcoming game, including Game Director Joe Shely, Narrative Director Jennifer Helper, and Production Director Tiffany Wat, who gave us tons of new details about Diablo 5, including how it’s already past early development.
IGN: I know probably nobody has missed the Diablo 5 announcement, but can you guys just kind of give sort of a top-level view of what the game will be?

Joe Shely: Diablo 5 is a world where Sanctuary has fallen and Diablo has won. That means that the world is in an apocalypse. The fate that players have been trying to prevent for many years throughout other Diablo games has happened. Other heroes rose up, tried to stop Diablo, and failed. Diablo sits on the throne of Westmarch and has conquered all of the Western continent.

articles.title: You’ll Fight The Protoss In StarCraft, Too, Don’t Worry
articles.summary: StarCraft's reveal trailer squarely put the focus on the Terrans, who later in the cinematic face a terrifying confrontation with the Zerg. The franchise's three franchises--including the Protoss--have always been a central element of what distinguishes StarCraft from other strategy games.
body: GameSpot spoke with GM and creative director Dan Hay at BlizzCon and asked him about how the three factions will interact with each other. Although he was expectedly coy on specifics, he did offer up some thoughts.

"The answer to that question is I absolutely unequivocally can't say," Hay said. "But what I can do is tell you what I would want as a player. I'll hint at sort of not what we're doing, but some of the things that we think about.

"Of course, what you want to be able to do... you think about the Protoss and how reverent we are. They're older, and there's a mystique and a grandness to them, right? They have just a completely different flavor. Then you have the Zerg, and the Zerg are just numberless; they're infinite from the standpoint of they just overwhelm you with sheer organic power. Then you have the Terrans, that are this group of... they're working their way through the sector in kind of a haphazard and industrial way. We want that feeling.

articles.title: The StarCraft Shooter Is A Third-Person Game, And Blizzard Insists That You Have To Feel “Powerful”
articles.summary: If you walked away from the StarCraft reveal excited for the franchise to return, but unsure what this new game even is, you're not alone. Aside from being described during the BlizzCon Opening Ceremony as an open-world shooter, Blizzard didn't share much else.
body: The StarCraft franchise, having taken the form of real-time strategy games previously, has typically used an isometric perspective. When it came to choosing what perspective to offer in the new shooter, it sounds like it wasn't a difficult decision.

"Oh, that's easy," Hay said when GameSpot asked him about whether StarCraft will be a first- or third-person game. "I want to be able to see my armor. First thing we did is we built it, put it on a turntable, and spun it around like, 'Ah, awesome, cool!' I want to be able to see it, so third-person, right?

"That doesn't mean that we don't have the license to, in a couple of spaces, do a little bit different and whatnot, but third-person: You get to see your armor, you get to see the full weight of everything you have, and then you get to see stuff that's in my head that I can't tell you."
points: If you walked away from the StarCraft reveal excited for the franchise to return, but unsure what this new game even is, you're not alone.

articles.title: Diablo 5 will fully support multiplayer, but Blizzard won't say how similar to Diablo 4 it'll be
articles.summary: Diablo 5 may be set in a lonely world ravaged by a demon lord, but you'll still be able to team up with your friends like in previous Diablo games. Senior game director Joe Shely confirmed that Diablo 5 will fully support multiplayer in a group interview with PC Gamer: "Like Diablo 4, it is a game…
body: Specific details about multiplayer, like if you can run into other players in the open world like you can in Diablo 4's endgame, weren't mentioned. Blizzard said that information will have to wait until we're closer to its 2029 release.

One of the biggest changes that differentiates Diablo 5 from Diablo 4 is its return to having a procedurally-generated overworld and dungeons. This is supposed to convey the shifting nature of the world as you travel across the continent with your caravan cleansing it of Diablo's corruption. It's possible that this might dramatically change how you'll interact with other players once you're finished with the campaign, especially if everyone experiences their own version of Sanctuary.

Running into a bunch of other players might ruin the illusion that you're a lone hero fighting back against the forces of Hell. Blizzard says Diablo 5 will incorporate a lot of things it learned from Diablo 4, but it's unclear if that will include things like world events and bosses. Diablo 4 is also overflowing with skins and cosmetics that, if carried forward, would suggest there must be some way of showing off your fit to the other heroes of Sanctuary.

articles.title: StarCraft Reboot Is “Focusing On Single-Player,” Creative Director Says
articles.summary: StarCraft is "focusing on single-player," StarCraft creative director and general manager Dan Hay and associate manager of development operations Anna Lee Hertling said in an interview with GameSpot.
body: One of the biggest announcements of BlizzCon 2026 was the return of StarCraft, described as an open-world shooter and slated for a 2030 release. Aside from its impressive reveal cinematic, there wasn't much additional information about how StarCraft would play or what the shooter reboot of the RTS franchise would entail.
Now, we have some more details. When asked whether StarCraft would be single-player or co-op, Hay said the team is "focusing on single player."

"We are focused right now on the conversation of focusing on single-player, focusing on that Marine fantasy, and then making sure that we think about what it is to be that character," Hay said. "That's what we're saying for now."

He said players will play as a named character that can "build a reputation and a rapport" with other in-game characters. He said the game's story will have a beginning, middle, and an "end," and that Blizzard wants it to feel like a "boxed product." Thought it's story will have an end, Hay said Blizzard wants the game to be one players can visit, explore, leave, and come back to.

articles.title: Blizzard Explains Why The StarCraft Shooter Coming In 2030 Was Announced Now
articles.summary: Thanks to rumors and reports, the announcement of a new StarCraft game taking the form of an open-world shooter did not come as a complete surprise at BlizzCon's Opening Ceremony. What is surprising is when it's coming: 2030.
body: Hay said that with Blizzard being confident in what it's developed so far, it didn't want to further delay going public and getting the benefit of putting it in front of fans.

"There's a moment when you're making a game where you're like, 'Have we landed the emotion? Do we feel like we have enough of the verve, the identity, and the feel of it to start to share it?'" Hay continued. "About a year ago, we started to feel like we were there, so we were like, 'Okay, it's time to show it. It's time to get feedback.'

"What's super important about it is you want to put it out there, get people to feel the emotion and the value of it, and you want to be there live to be able to get a sense of how they feel about it. We were in the room; it felt great. People were going nuts."
